abstract: A rational Diophantine tuple has pairwise products plus one square, and an entry is strong when its square plus one is square. We prove twelve coordinate exclusions in the elliptic square-product quintuple families of Dujella, Kazalicki and Petričević: A, B, C and D in families 1 and 2, and A, B, D and E in family 3. Combined with an earlier C exclusion, thirteen of the fifteen cases are excluded and no valid quintuple in family 3 has a strong coordinate. Five exclusions use finite square-class descent and genus-two curves with rank-one Jacobians. Four use genus-four curves with rank-three Jacobians: one admits a complete eight-point classification, while inherited square conditions isolate the degenerate points needed on the other. A smaller genus-three quotient has rank at least three, explaining an ordinary Chabauty obstruction. Another pair follows from a complete sixteen-point classification on a diagonal genus-five curve. Certified twist descent reduces it to a rank-one elliptic cover over the quadratic field of discriminant 105, where saturation and elliptic Chabauty determine all rational parameter values. The final exclusion uses a genus-two point-class sieve to obtain a rank-one elliptic cover over a quintic field; etale logarithms eliminate mixed local sign patterns and leave only poles. All original parameter maps, poles and zeros are checked exactly. The supplement provides unconditional number-field certificates, complete local square-class computations, precision-controlled logarithms, and independent checks at different primes or by different formulas. These results constrain a route toward tuples containing a product-minus-one pair without settling arbitrary strong square-product quintuples, square-product sextuples, or rational Diophantine septuples.

change_summary: Adds seven coordinate exclusions to the five in version1, yielding twelve proved here and thirteen with the earlier C3 result. Section8 proves the full eight-point genus-four classification for family3 A/D, with rank-three descent, a genus-three rank barrier, and independent 7-adic/5-adic certificates. Section9 excludes family2 B/C using a second rank-three genus-four Jacobian and independent restricted-point proofs at 11 and 7. Section10 classifies a diagonal genus-five curve and excludes family1 B/C through complete twist descent, a rank-one quadratic-field elliptic cover, exact 2-saturation and 13-adic Chabauty. Section11 excludes family1 A through a complete genus-two point-class sieve, full 2-descent over a quintic field, and etale elliptic Chabauty at 11. All new coordinate maps and exceptions are checked exactly. Updated abstract, theorem, scope, literature comparison and contributions. Only E1 and E2 remain unresolved in the fifteen-case list. Clarified necessary-descent rank bounds and version-specific citations in response to the version1 review.

coauthors.contribution: Independently established all five rank bounds and checked coordinate maps, eligible residue discs and exact Cantor arithmetic; supplied compact B/E Hilbert-symbol certificates and reviewed the descent conventions and manuscript. For the new genus-four theorem, found and certified the retained-square rank bound, proved the genus-three rank barrier, supplied an independent 5-adic proof, and independently reproduced the full 7-adic classification and parameter exclusions. For family2 B/C, established the genus-four descent bound, supplied the independent 7-adic proof, and audited the inherited-square lemma and the complete 11-adic argument. For family1 B/C, independently reproduced the complete twist descent, rank bound, saturation and Chabauty certificates, supplied an independent formal-log calculation and factor-twist sieve, and audited the global support proof. For family1 A, constructed the fixed quintic-field elliptic cover, established the complete point-class sieve and rank-one descent, and supplied the etale Chabauty theorem and exact maps.
